clue.text: Discharged about everyone in the plant

indicators.note: about says the word for discharged goes round the word for everyone

parts.note: a gun discharged has shot
everyone means all

explanation.surface: Someone fired a weapon at all the workers in a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ALL inside SHOT. 'plant' looks like a factory, but it is the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: The shallot is a small onion-like bulb grown in vegetable gardens.

clue.text: Vehicle gets upset by river — girl gets writ

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word for vehicle is turned upside down

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle
the Po is the great river of northern Italy
Ena is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl gets served legal papers after a bus tips over near a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A subpoena is a court order commanding someone to appear as a witness.

clue.text: A writer figures on seeing mountains

parts.note: a pen is a thing that writes
nines are figures, digits

explanation.surface: An author tots up numbers while gazing at a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apennines are the mountain chain running down the length of Italy.

clue.text: Binds — at punishment on the Bounty?

explanation.surface: A question whether the floggings aboard the famous mutiny ship were tied up.
explanation.definitionFit: Lashes are ties, as for securing with rope, and strokes of the whip, as flogging was used on HMS Bounty, scene of a famous mutiny.

clue.text: The point of defining time

parts.note: taken as written
N is north, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: The purpose behind defining what time is.
explanation.definitionFit: Then means at that time, a moment in the past or future.

clue.text: Politicians liable to be locked up

explanation.surface: Members of the government might end up in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior ministers form a governing body, and a cupboard with a door often has a lock and key.

clue.text: Poet gives quick talk on fashion

parts.note: chatter is rapid idle talk
ton is an old word for fashion or style

explanation.surface: A versifier talks rapidly about the latest styles.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Chatterton was an eighteenth-century English poet who died at seventeen.

clue.text: He's not half stewed !

parts.note: not half means he lacks a better half, a wife, and so has to cook his own stew

explanation.definitionFit: An unmarried man has no wife, the partner sometimes called his better half.

clue.text: Rugby footballer brought up in Belgium ?

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue says the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: RU stands for Rugby Union
a footballer is a man in the team

explanation.surface: A rugby player was raised in Belgium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns RU MAN to read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Namur is a city in Wallonia, southern Belgium, where two rivers meet.

clue.text: Commotion about the French in a Spanish city

indicators.note: about says the word for commotion goes round the French article

parts.note: a to-do is a fuss or commotion
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A disturbance concerning the French breaks out in a city in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Toledo is a historic walled city in central Spain, famed for its swords.

clue.text: Does this Israel town drink to part of Arabia?

parts.note: beer is a common drink
Sheba was the ancient kingdom in southern Arabia, home of its biblical queen

explanation.surface: A question whether the people of an Israeli town raise a toast to an Arabian region.
explanation.definitionFit: Beersheba is a city in the Negev desert of southern Israel.

clue.text: Arrived at Leatherhead — by this transport?

parts.note: to have arrived at a place is to have come to it
the head of the word Leather is its first letter, L; the Surrey town Leatherhead is the disguise

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone reached a Surrey town riding a desert animal.
explanation.walkthrough: Leatherhead is a town in Surrey, south of London; here it is read as 'leather head', the first letter of leather.
explanation.definitionFit: The camel is the beast of burden that carries riders and loads across deserts.

clue.text: Possibly Sue conformed with these measures

indicators.note: possibly says the letters might be arranged some other way

parts.note: the word splits as con plus formed: the opening three letters are the fodder, and formed backs up the rearranging

explanation.surface: Perhaps a woman called Sue followed these rules.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'conformed' as 'con formed': SUE and CON, 'possibly' rearranged, are formed into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ounces are small units of weight in the imperial system.

clue.text: Girl got danger signal-wasn't ready

definitions.note: a phrase describing a person, standing for the English king known as the Unready

parts.note: Ethel is a girl's name
a red light or flag signals danger

explanation.surface: A girl saw a red warning light and was caught unprepared.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to the Anglo-Saxon king Ethelred the Unready, so 'wasn't ready' describes him.
explanation.definitionFit: The Saxon king Ethelred II is known to history by the nickname 'the Unready'.

clue.text: Plant presented to proud father ?

explanation.surface: Flowers given to a man whose baby has just been born.
explanation.definitionFit: Storksbill is a wild flower whose fruit resembles a bird's beak, and folklore has the stork delivering babies with its beak.

clue.text: Number 2 section

indicators.note: section says a run of letters is cut out of the middle of that entry

parts.note: the answer to 2 down, the mountain range

explanation.surface: A bare reference to a numbered part of a document.
explanation.walkthrough: The '2' is the answer to 2 down, and a section of its letters gives the number.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine is a cardinal number, three times three.

clue.text: Remark about changes in town or port

indicators.note: about puts the word for remark round the rearranged letters

parts.note: to remark is to say

indicators.note: changes in says the letters of town or are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A comment on how things are changing in some town or harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes in' rearranges TOWN OR into TORNOW, and 'about' wraps SAY round it. Stornoway is the main port of the Isle of Lewis in the Scottish Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: Stornoway is a harbour town in the Outer Hebrides, a ferry and fishing port.

clue.text: One had tomorrow

parts.note: had means tricked, so the clue reads as a person who will be fooled on the following day

explanation.walkthrough: 'had' is slang for tricked or fooled, so the clue describes the victim of a prank on 1 April, the day after 31 March.
explanation.definitionFit: The victim of a prank played on the first of April is given this name.

clue.text: Need about half the band up in the City

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the whole run of letters is read from the bottom

parts.note: taken as written
re means about, concerning

indicators.note: half takes the opening two of the four letters of band

explanation.surface: Wanting a few musicians to appear in town.
explanation.walkthrough: NEED, RE and BA (half of 'band') together are turned by 'up' to read ABERDEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdeen is a granite city on the north-east coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Sort of bed, of course !

explanation.surface: A kind of bed, naturally!
explanation.definitionFit: An apple-pie bed is a prank where sheets are folded so the sleeper cannot stretch out, and apple pie is a dessert, a course of a meal.

clue.text: Wood meets melancholy anatomist in Devon

parts.note: ash is a tree and its timber
Robert Burton wrote The Anatomy of Melancholy (1621)

explanation.surface: A tree meets a gloomy dissecting scientist somewhere in a West Country county.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'anatomist' is not a surgeon: Robert Burton wrote The Anatomy of Melancholy. Devon is a county in south-west England, and the answer is a town in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashburton is a small market town on the edge of Dartmoor, in the English county of Devon.

clue.text: Stay for piano

parts.note: pro means for, as in pros and cons
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A request to remain on behalf of the pianist.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay is a support, as is a prop holding something up.

clue.text: Girl raises first-class fruit

indicators.note: raises in a down clue says the letters run upwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written here as the letters A and I
a lime is a fruit

explanation.surface: A girl grows top-quality fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raises' turns A1 LIME upwards, with the figure 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Emilia is a girl's name, as in the character in Othello.

clue.text: Room for development in one modern version

definitions.text: Room for development in one modern version

parts.words: Room for development in one modern version
parts.note: the Latin word for room or chamber names the device in which film is exposed for developing, the modern sense of the old word

explanation.walkthrough: The Latin camera meant a vaulted room, as in 'in camera' or camera obscura, a darkened room; the modern device holds film for development.
explanation.definitionFit: The photographic device takes its name from the Latin for chamber, from camera obscura, a dark room.

clue.text: Suspect damp and decay

parts.note: mist is damp air
rust is the decay of iron

explanation.surface: Wariness of damp weather and its corroding effects.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspect someone is to doubt them, to lack trust in them.

clue.text: Painful part of quarrels or estrangements

definitions.note: an adjective, standing for a plural noun naming painful places

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Arguments and rifts cause hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Sores are tender, inflamed patches of skin that hurt.

clue.text: Spanish composer gets a pound for a trifle

parts.note: Manuel de Falla was a Spanish composer
L is the abbreviation for pound, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: A Spanish musician is paid a pound for a small thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A fal-lal is a showy trinket or piece of finery of little worth.

clue.text: Only a point up in the end

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: but means only, as in but a child
S is south, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Just one point gained at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns BUT S into STUB; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stub is the short end left over, as of a pencil or cigarette.

clue.text: Is right, in a way, in N. Ireland

indicators.note: in says the letter for right is placed inside the word for a way

parts.note: a lane is a way or narrow road

explanation.surface: Something is correct, after a fashion, in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts R into LANE. 'Is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Larne is a port town in County Antrim, Northern Ireland, with ferries to Scotland.

clue.text: Having difficulty with nuts? Hope I can arrange it

indicators.note: arrange it asks for the letters of nuts and hope I to be put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone struggling with a bag of nuts hopes to sort them out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrange' shuffles the letters of NUTS and HOPE I.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in trouble or a fix is an idiom for being in a difficult spot.

clue.text: A magazine club ?

explanation.surface: Asking whether a periodical belongs to a society.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsenal is a store of weapons and ammunition, a sense of magazine, and Arsenal is a London football team.

clue.text: Touch type

parts.note: read as type, a script, that is read by touch rather than the typing skill

explanation.definitionFit: Braille is the raised-dot writing that blind people read with their fingertips.
